newsitem.title: USA: Greenspan denies trying to talk down stock market.
newsitem.headline: Greenspan denies trying to talk down stock market.

text.p: Federal Reserve Chairman denied again on Wednesday that he was trying to talk down the stock market when he suggested last week and in December that equity prices may be too high.
"You cannot do it even if you would like to," he told the National Association of Business Economists. "There is no way you can talk down or talk up prices or interest rates."
The Fed chief has come in for some sharp criticism for his comments from investors and analysts who have accused him of meddling in a market in which he has no business doing so.

Greenspan though defended his comments, saying that the Fed needed to take account of what he called "balance sheet forces" because of their increasing importance in trying to gauge the future direction of the economy.

"We (the Fed) no longer have got the capability of waiting until we see events evolve," Greenspan said. "Monetary policy which is not forward-looking is monetary policy which is ultimately counter-productive."
"Unless we look at the increasing evidence that balance sheet impacts matter, then I think we are missing the boat in the way we construct monetary policy," Greenspan added.

He first raised the issue in December of whether the markets were infected with "irrational exuberance," then took up the question more pointedly in his Humphrey-Hawkins testimony to the Senate Banking Committee last week.
The Fed Chairman said he would repeat that testimony to a House Banking subcommittee later today.
On the subject of economic indicators, Greenspan again asserted that the Consumer Price Index was upwardly biased, although he said it was not the only piece of government data that was flawed.
The Fed chief urged Congress to allocate more money for the improvement of the CPI and other data and said better statistics were an important part of the process of attempting to balance the budget.
"If our purpose is to get balanced budgets and a rational fiscal system, a good data system is in my judgment a necessary condition," he said.
